land.text: the Livonian branch's lands in Latvia and Estonia, drawn inside the Teutonic Order's Cliopatria shape to 1421

predecessors.note: The Livonian Order was 'a semi-autonomous branch' of the Teutonic Knights from 1237; Cliopatria sets it apart in 1422. The confederation agreement was signed at Walk on 4 December 1435.

land.text: 'Livonia north of the Daugava was subordinated directly to Sigismund II Augustus as Duchy of Livonia'

successors.note: Treaty of Vilnius, 28 November 1561; Poland-Lithuania also took Courland and Semigallia as a hereditary fief held by Kettler. Cliopatria's House of Jagiellon row runs to 1571.

land.text: 'Courland and Semigallia was thus made a hereditary fief of the Grand Duke of Lithuania'

successors.note: Kettler's duchy, 1561; the Cliopatria row 'Duchy of Courland' covers only 1734-1793, so the duchy's first 170 years have no row.

land.text: Reval and the Estonian corporations of Harrien-Wierland and Jerwen, which yielded to Sweden in 1561

successors.note: Livonian War page: 'Estonia to Kingdom of Sweden'.

land.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek (Ösel/Saaremaa, Dagö/Hiiumaa, Wiek/Lääne)

successors.note: Bought by Frederick II of Denmark in 1559 (sale of 26 September 1559); Duke Magnus took possession in April 1560.

land.text: Dorpat (Tartu) and Narva, taken in 1558, and Fellin (Viljandi), taken in 1560

successors.note: Held until the Truce of Jam Zapolski in 1582 ('Russia lost all of its former holdings').

capitals.name: Wenden (Cēsis)
capitals.note: The Confederation had no capital: the Archbishop of Riga was its nominal head and the Diet met at Walk (Valga, 'gathered in 1419'). Wenden was the Livonian Order's seat (infobox 'Wenden (Cēsis) and Fellin (Viljandi)'; Plettenberg died at Wenden Castle on 28 February 1535).

keyframe_review.note: 116,338 km2: Latvia and Estonia (Estonia 223 of 228 cells, Latvia 303 of 314). The Terra Mariana page gives 'about 67,000 km2' for the Livonian Order and 'about 41,000 km2' for the Church by the mid-14th century (about 108,000 km2 together), so Cliopatria's figure is within 10%. The Diet 'gathered in 1419'; the confederation agreement at Walk is dated 4 December 1435, and the Livonian Order stayed independent after Grunwald (1410) because it did not take part. Note: the Wolter von Plettenberg page says Harju County, Virumaa and Tallinn came under the Livonian Master's direct control in 1525, having been 'under the Prussian Grand Master' before; see notes.

116,497 km2: the same lands (a 160 km2 difference). The 1501-1503 war with Muscovy ended 'on the terms of status quo ante bellum' (the 1503 truce, renewed in 1509, 1521 and 1531), so no frontier moved.

116,393 km2: the same lands. In 1525-1526 Plettenberg 'rejected conversion to Lutheranism and secularization of the Livonian Order' and was made a Prince of the Empire (1526, confirmed 1530); the Confederation kept its autonomy.

116,393 km2, drawn whole to 1563. The Livonian War began on 22 January 1558 and the land was partitioned before 1563 (Dorpat and Narva to Russia in 1558, Ösel to Denmark in 1559-60, northern Estonia to Sweden in 1561, the Treaty of Vilnius on 28 November 1561), so the shape is right only for 1556-1557; new keyframes follow for 1558, 1559 and 1561.

correction.text: Livonia without Dorpat and Narva, taken by the Russians in 1558

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Russian troops took Dorpat (Tartu) in May, Narva in July' 1558 (a footnote swaps the two months). Dorpat is read as the county of Tartu, Narva as a 30 km radius.

correction.text: Livonia without Dorpat, Narva and the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek (Saare, Hiiu, Lääne), 1559

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Bishop Johann von Münchhausen 'signed a treaty on 26 September 1559' giving Frederick II of Denmark the right to nominate the bishop of Ösel-Wiek, 'a sale'; Duke Magnus 'then took possession in April 1560'. The bishopric is read as the counties of Saare, Hiiu and Lääne (Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek page: 'what are now Saare, Hiiu, Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county'). Valid for 1559 only; Fellin falls in 1560 (next keyframe). (Review 2026-10-25: Ösel was Saare only and the keyframe ran 1559-1560.)

correction.text: Livonia without Dorpat, Narva, the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek and Fellin (Viljandi), 1560

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review 2026-10-25): the Viljandi page: 'in 1560, the forces of Knyaz Andrey Kurbsky of Muscovite Russia succeeded in seizing' Fellin; the Livonian War page dates the defeat at Ērģeme to August 1560 and has 'The Tsar's forces took important fortresses like Fellin (Viljandi)'. Fellin is read as the county of Viljandi. Other fortresses lost in 1560 (the page names none) are not drawn.

correction.text: Livonia without Dorpat, Narva, the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek, Fellin and northern Estonia, until 28 November 1561

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1561, Swedish forces arrived and the noble corporations of Harrien-Wierland and Jerwen yielded to Sweden' (Reval in the same passage); the remainder, Livonia north of the Daugava and Courland and Semigallia, passed to Poland-Lithuania on 28 November 1561 (Treaty of Vilnius), ending the Order. Cliopatria keeps the whole shape to 1563.

region.text: Livonia: Latvia and Estonia under the Order, the archbishop and the bishops

ledger.note: 1422: the Livonian lands stand apart from the Teutonic Order. Cliopatria starts a separate row in 1422, the year of the Treaty of Melno; the pages opened date no 1422 event: the Livonian Order is 'a semi-autonomous branch' from 1237, 'the Livonian Diet gathered in 1419' and the confederation agreement is of 4 December 1435. The Treaty of Melno page (27 September 1422) says the Samogitian strip 'separated the Teutonic Knights in Prussia from their branch in Livonia' but names no constitutional separation, so the year stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

4 December 1435: the Livonian Confederation agreement is signed at Walk. 'The confederation agreement was signed in Walk on 4 December 1435 by the Archbishop of Riga, the bishops, the Order and vassal representatives, and deputies from Riga, Reval, and Dorpat' (Order page: 'From 1435 to 1561, it was a member of the Livonian Confederation').

1558: Dorpat and Narva fall to the Russians. 'Russian troops took Dorpat (Tartu) in May, Narva in July'; a footnote cites De Madariaga: 'Narva in May and Dorpat in July'. The Russians held them until the Truce of Jam Zapolski in 1582.

region.text: the Dorpat and Narva districts, where the Russian armies first took ground

ledger.note: 22 January 1558: Ivan IV invades Livonia. 'On 22 January 1558, Ivan reacted with the invasion of Livonia.' Dorpat and Narva fall in May and July (the page's text and a footnote disagree on which came first).

region.text: the Order's lands under the protection of the Polish king and Grand Duke of Lithuania

ledger.note: 31 August 1559: the first Treaty of Vilnius puts Livonia under Polish-Lithuanian protection. 'With the Treaty of Vilnius of 31 August 1559' the Order's lands were put 'under protection of Polish king and Grand Duke of Lithuania, Sigismund II Augustus' (Treaty of Vilnius (1561) page). The Livonian War page gives June 1559 ('the estates of Livonia came under Polish-Lithuanian protection through the first Treaty of Vilnius'); house-of-jagiellon ledger has vassal_start 1559-6 for livonian-conference, so the months differ by two. (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

region.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek: 'what are now Saare, Hiiu, Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county of Estonia'

ledger.note: 26 September 1559: the Bishop of Ösel-Wiek sells to Denmark. Bishop Johann von Münchhausen 'signed a treaty on 26 September 1559', giving Frederick II the right to nominate the bishop, 'which amounted to a sale' for 30,000 thalers; Duke Magnus took possession in April 1560 (15 April 1560 on the Ösel-Wiek page, whose infobox dates the sale 1560). The land is the whole bishopric, not Ösel alone: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek page says it covered 'what are now Saare, Hiiu, Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county'; the western Pärnu part is not drawn. Pilten in the Bishopric of Courland, which denmark-norway's 1559 gain also names, is not here: the Livonian War page does not link Courland or Pilten to the 1559 treaty (Magnus 'later' bought the Bishopric of Courland) and the Magnus of Livonia page gives no date for it; the denmark-norway author should drop or date it. (Review 2026-10-25: region was Saare only.)

region.text: Fellin (Viljandi) and its county, where the Russian armies took ground in 1560

ledger.note: 1560: the Russian campaign reaches Fellin. 'in 1560, the forces of Knyaz Andrey Kurbsky of Muscovite Russia succeeded in seizing' Viljandi (Viljandi page, year only); the Livonian War page: 'The Livonian knights suffered a disastrous defeat by the Russians at the Battle of Ērģeme in August 1560' (2 August 1560 on the Battle of Ērģeme page, which does not mention Fellin) and 'The Tsar's forces took important fortresses like Fellin (Viljandi)', undated. Year-only, no month: the Viljandi page gives none. (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

1560: Fellin (Viljandi) falls to the Russians. The Viljandi page: 'in 1560, the forces of Knyaz Andrey Kurbsky of Muscovite Russia succeeded in seizing' it; the Livonian War page: 'The Tsar's forces took important fortresses like Fellin (Viljandi)'. The region is the researcher's reading (the county of Viljandi); duchy-of-livonia's ledger has Dorpat and Fellin held by Russia in 1561. (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

1561: northern Estonia yields to Sweden. 'In 1561, Swedish forces arrived and the noble corporations of Harrien-Wierland and Jerwen yielded to Sweden'; Reval 'accepted Swedish rule' in the same passage, without its own date.

region.text: Livonia north of the Daugava, the Duchy of Livonia

ledger.note: 28 November 1561: the Livonian Order is secularised and Livonia passes to Poland-Lithuania. 'In November 1561 the new Grand Master Gotthard Kettler secularized the Order and surrendered Livonia to Sigismund Augustus'; 'Livonia north of the Daugava was subordinated directly to Sigismund II Augustus as Duchy of Livonia'.

28 November 1561: Courland and Semigallia become Kettler's duchy under Poland-Lithuania. 'Courland and Semigallia was thus made a hereditary fief of the Grand Duke of Lithuania, later of the Polish Crown'; Kettler held it as duke and 'Polish-Lithuanian vassal'.

28 November 1561: the Confederation ceases to exist, so its fight with Russia ends here. The Livonian War itself ran on between Russia, Poland-Lithuania, Sweden and Denmark until the Truce of Jam Zapolski (1582) and the Truce of Plussa (10 August 1583); the Order was 'dissolved by the second Treaty of Vilnius in 1561'.

28 November 1561: the Confederation ceases to exist, so its fight with Russia over Fellin ends with it (as for Dorpat and Narva, previous event). Fellin stayed Russian; duchy-of-livonia carries the contest from 1561. (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

region.text: the lands of the Livonian Order under Polish-Lithuanian protection

ledger.note: 28 November 1561: the protection ends with the second Treaty of Vilnius ('The Treaty of Vilnius was concluded on 28 November 1561'; the page does not say in so many words that the protection ended). The Order is secularised and Livonia is annexed as the Duchy of Livonia; house-of-jagiellon ledger has vassal_end 1561-11 for livonian-conference. (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

28 November 1561: the Livonian Confederation ends. 'The Treaty of Vilnius was concluded on 28 November 1561'; the Livonian War page: 'The weakened Livonian Order was dissolved by the second Treaty of Vilnius in 1561'; the Terra Mariana page: 'In 1561, during the Livonian War, Terra Mariana ceased to exist'. Riga, excluded, became a free imperial city; Cliopatria draws the shape to 1563.

wars.name: Russo-Livonian War (1501-1503)
wars.outcome: Plettenberg won the Battle of Lake Smolina on 13 September 1502; after the defeat at Helme and the failed siege of Pskov 'peace between Ivan III and Livonia on the terms of status quo ante bellum was concluded' in 1503 (a six-year truce, renewed 1509, 1521, 1531).
wars.note: The page gives no date for Helme or the siege of Pskov; no frontier moved.

wars.name: Livonian War
wars.outcome: The Livonian Confederation was partitioned in 1559-1561 (the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek to Denmark-Norway, Fellin to Russia 1560, Estonia to Sweden, Livonia, Courland and Semigallia to Poland-Lithuania); the war ran to the Truce of Jam Zapolski (1582, Russia lost 'all of its former holdings') and the Truce of Plussa with Sweden (10 August 1583).
wars.note: Infobox: 22 January 1558 - 10 August 1583. Livonian knights were defeated at Ērģeme in August 1560 (2 August on the Battle of Ērģeme page); Fellin fell in 1560 (Viljandi page). The first Treaty of Vilnius put the Order's lands under Sigismund II Augustus's protection (31 August 1559 on the Treaty of Vilnius (1561) page, 'June 1559' on this page; ledger vassal_start/vassal_end now carry it). Reviewer 2026-10-25: 'to' set to 1561, the confederation's end (the war itself ran to 1583).

certainty.note: Cliopatria draws the Confederation as whole modern Latvia and Estonia; the lands of the Order, the archbishop and the bishops were intermixed, and the eastern frontier on the Narva and Lake Peipus was fixed only as 'status quo ante bellum' in 1503.
A shifting front of the Livonian War; the 28 November 1561 Treaty of Vilnius is a treaty line only on paper.

notes: Pages: 5 opened (budget 5; the Livonian Confederation URL returned the Terra Mariana article, and the Russo-Livonian War URLs 'Russo-Livonian_War_(1501-1503)' and 'Russo-Livonian_War' did not load). The Cliopatria Wikipedia title ('Livonian language') and Wikidata id (Q33698) are the language's, not the state's; this dossier gives 'Livonian Confederation' as the article but keeps Q33698 because the schema takes Cliopatria's id. Start 1422 is Cliopatria's row boundary (page silent); the pages date the Diet to 1419 and the Confederation to 4 December 1435. End 1561 (28 November) against Cliopatria's 1563. The Livonian War partition is drawn by the new keyframes 1558, 1559 and 1561 and their ledger events. Unsettled: the Wolter von Plettenberg page says 'In 1525 ... Harju County, Virumaa, and Tallinn came under his direct control. These had previously been under the Prussian Grand Master', i.e. that northern Estonia was the Teutonic Order's own until 1525, while the Livonian Order page says the Livonian order bought Estonia in 1346 and the State of the Teutonic Order page says the Teutonic Order did. Cliopatria draws Estonia in the Livonian row from 1422; no gain was recorded for 1525 because one page alone says so; a gap-filler should check it (the Teutonic Order dossier would then keep Estonia 1422-1525). Other dossiers needed: the first Treaty of Vilnius (31 August 1559 on the Treaty of Vilnius (1561) page, June 1559 on the Livonian War page; protection under Sigismund II Augustus) is now a vassal_start/vassal_end here and in house-of-jagiellon (1559-6 to 1561-11), counterpart livonian-conference; the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia (1561-1795) has no Cliopatria row before 1734 and needs a duchy-of-courland dossier starting in 1561; the Duchy of Livonia (1561-1569/1621) and Riga (a free imperial city, then Polish from 1581) have no rows. The Archbishopric of Riga, the Bishoprics of Dorpat, Ösel-Wiek and Courland and the Livonian Order are inside this one state. No ruler list, since only the last Masters were seen. Gazetteer: 'Old Livonia' and 'Livonia' resolve (246 of 249 'Livonia' cells lie in the Cliopatria shape). REVIEW REPAIRS 2026-10-25 (author). Applied: vassal_start 1559-8 and vassal_end 1561-11 (counterpart house-of-jagiellon); Fellin (Viljandi county) lost to Russia in 1560 (confidence 2: the Viljandi page gives the year, the Livonian War page 'took important fortresses like Fellin' without a date; a second contest pair for the zone and keyframe livonian-conference_1560, carried into 1561); the 1559 sale now takes the whole Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek (counties Saare, Hiiu, Lääne) in the ledger, keyframes and the Danish successor; the 1559 keyframe runs 1559 only. Disagreement: the first Treaty of Vilnius is 31 August 1559 on the Treaty of Vilnius (1561) page and June 1559 on the Livonian War page (the earlier note's 31 August did not come from the war page); I used the dated treaty (month 8) and house-of-jagiellon has month 6. Not done: Pilten (Bishopric of Courland) is not added to the 1559 loss, because the Livonian War page says only that Magnus 'later' bought the Bishopric of Courland and the Magnus of Livonia and Ösel-Wiek pages give no date or mention of Pilten; denmark-norway's 1559 gain names 'Courland's Pilten' at confidence 2 and should be dated or dropped by its author. The western part of Pärnu county, also in the bishopric, is not drawn. Thin items: the 1422 start stays confidence 1 (the Treaty of Melno page says the Samogitian strip 'separated the Teutonic Knights in Prussia from their branch in Livonia' and nothing about a split); the Russo-Livonian War (1501-1503) pages failed again under 'Russo-Livonian_War_(1501%E2%80%931503)', 'Battle_of_Smolino' and 'Battle_of_Lake_Smolino', so wars/0 keeps the Plettenberg page. The Harrien-Wierland question is open (see teutonic-order notes).
